$comment: Shared, language-neutral block trees for the Blade-vs-JS markup parity check (#704). Consumed by both packages/visual-editor-renderer-blade/tests/Feature/RendererMarkupParityTest.php (PHP) and packages/renderer-markup-parity/tests/blade-parity.test.ts (JS). Adding a fixture here automatically exercises it against all three renderers. See README.md for the golden-file workflow.

knownDivergences.reason: Element ids differ by design. Blade mints `ap-modal-nav-N` (container) and `ap-modal-nav-N-content` from NavigationOverlayTracker so its inline script can find the drawer; React's container id comes from `useId()` (SSR-safe, `:R…:`); Vue sets none (the `^3.3` peer has no `useId`). The id values can never match, so `id` is dropped inside navigation overlay fixtures only.

RN-5: the open button's `aria-controls` points at the renderer's own container id (Blade tracker id, React `useId()`); Vue omits it because it has no SSR-stable id. The value is renderer-specific by construction. `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-label` are still compared.

Blade-only `data-ap-nav-overlay-open` / `-close` / `-backdrop` hooks wire the delegated inline toggle script; React and Vue bind the same behavior with component event handlers, so they have no hook attributes.

Blade emits the overlay fix-up CSS and the toggle controller once per response as attribute-less inline `<style>` and `<script>` after the first overlay nav. React and Vue need no script (component state) and ship their CSS in `<style data-ve-navigation-overlay>` (declared separately).

React/Vue inject `NAVIGATION_OVERLAY_CSS` (block-library overlay subset + the Blade fix-ups, in `@layer ve-navigation`) because JS hosts are not required to load the block-library stylesheet; Blade relies on its bundled style.css plus the inline fix-ups. The bodies differ by design, so the tag is dropped rather than compared as per-instance CSS.

Blade reads the modern flex-layout `layout.orientation` (falling back to the legacy top-level `orientation`); React/Vue read only `orientation` and default to `is-horizontal`, so a `layout.orientation: vertical` nav renders `is-vertical` only in Blade.
Blade honors `layout.justifyContent` (Keystone #52, winning over legacy `itemsJustification`); React/Vue read only `itemsJustification`, so `items-justified-*` from the modern path is Blade-only.

Nav-level `customTextColor` / `customBackgroundColor` (Keystone #53) are rendered — sanitized through `safeCssValue` — only by Blade; React/Vue do not render them at all, so `has-text-color` / `has-background` on the `<nav>` are Blade-only.
The inline `color` / `background-color` declarations those nav-level custom colors produce on the `<nav>` are Blade-only for the same reason; the only `style` attribute in this fixture is the nav's.

`ElementsSupport` (Elements API link color, `style.elements.link.color.text`) is compiled only by the Blade partial into a per-block `wp-elements-{hash}` scope class; the JS renderers have no ElementsSupport.

The scoped `.wp-elements-{hash} a:where(:not(.wp-element-button)) { color: … }` rules ElementsSupport pushes into the shared `<style data-ve-elements>` block (#852) — Blade-only, like its scope class.
